body.statement: For the Clopper--Pearson preliminary region \(C_n\), profile discrepancy \(\Delta_n\), and Berger--Boos calibration in \(\operatorname{pv}_n\), \(P_{\vartheta}\{\tau(\vartheta)\in K_n\}\ge 1-\alpha\) at every sample size for every \(\vartheta\) in either design. The bound holds along arbitrary sequences approaching \(\mathfrak D\), including point-to-set transitions. Uniformly over compact subsets of \(\mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}\), \(\sqrt n\,d_{\mathrm H}(K_n,W_n)\xrightarrow{P}0\); equivalently, the local profile boundary and the Wald ellipse have the same first-order quadratic expansion and \(\chi^2_{2,1-\alpha}\) calibration. At any law with a non-singleton identified set or without the separated-chart conditions, the theorem asserts coverage only and makes no claim that \(\operatorname{diam}(K_n)\) shrinks.
body.justification: Exact nuisance calibration preserves coverage at transitions, while the explicit Hausdorff comparison recovers ordinary Wald geometry on separated charts.
body.gap: Existing weak-identification and stable-bound procedures do not calibrate a profile discrepancy over this changing selected-SCM fiber or establish its first-order agreement with chart-specific Wald inference.
body.consumer: Boundary-sensitive PN/PS analyses receive honest uncertainty without interpreting a nonshrinking confidence fiber as point identification.

obligation.what_is_open: The uniform first-order Hausdorff equivalence between the exact profile confidence fiber and the selected Wald ellipse on the globally defined atlas.
obligation.obstruction: Finite-sample coverage is exact without the atlas, but the Hausdorff assertion requires a uniform quadratic profile expansion over all incident glued charts and proof that the compiler omits no nearby mixed-support component.
obligation.attempted: Berger--Boos coverage was proved by the preliminary-region event and exact super-uniform tail values; the regular local quadratic reduction was derived conditional on atlas exhaustiveness.
obligation.partial_result:
The finite-sample coverage part does not require rank stability.  Let \(q_0\) be the true observable law and \(t_0=\tau(\vartheta)\).  Inversion of each binomial tail makes its two-sided Clopper--Pearson interval miss its true cell probability with probability no greater than its allocated error.  Bonferroni therefore gives
\[
P_{q_0}(q_0\notin C_n)\le\beta_n.
\]
For fixed \((q,t)\) with \(t\in\mathcal T(q)\), the exact upper-tail randomization value
\[
G_{q,t}=P_q\{\Delta_n^{\mathrm{rep}}(t)\ge\Delta_n^{\mathrm{obs}}(t)\}
\]
is super-uniform under \(q\): for every \(u\in[0,1]\), \(P_q(G_{q,t}\le u)\le u\), including at atoms.  On \(\{q_0\in C_n\}\), the supremum defining \(\operatorname{pv}_n(t_0)\) contains \(q_0\), so
\[
\operatorname{pv}_n(t_0)\ge\min\{1,\beta_n+G_{q_0,t_0}\}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
P_{q_0}\{t_0\notin K_n\}
\le P_{q_0}(q_0\notin C_n)+P_{q_0}(G_{q_0,t_0}\le\alpha-\beta_n)
\le\beta_n+(\alpha-\beta_n)=\alpha.
\]
This proves exact coverage, uniformly along arbitrary transition sequences.  On a locally exhaustive separated smooth chart, a quadratic multinomial likelihood expansion and the common incident Jacobian reduce the profile deviance to the Wald quadratic up to \(o_P(1)\), which would imply \(\sqrt n,d_{\mathrm H}(K_n,W_n)\to0\).  The unresolved part is a uniform glued-chart profile expansion after proving that no mixed-support component is omitted by the compiler.
